title: Holding Step for Long-Held and Part-Paid Pieces
content:
# Bench Standing Order: The Holding Step for Long-Held and Part-Paid Pieces

## How the holding time is measured

The time a piece has been in the chain's hands under the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service is counted from the day it was taken in over the counter to the handling date. Where it is compared with the level's target turnaround, that target turnaround is counted in calendar days, taking 7 calendar days to 5 working days.

## The step

Where the piece has been in the chain's hands longer than the level's target turnaround and a payment already stands on the work order, the long holding step of 9 percent is added to the basis figure.

Where exactly one of those two holds — the piece held longer than that turnaround with no payment standing on the order, or a payment standing on the order with the piece held no longer than that turnaround — the standing holding step of 4 percent is added.

In any other case no step is added on this ground.

| Held longer than the level's target turnaround | A payment stands on the work order | Step added |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | 9 percent |
| yes | no | 4 percent |
| no | yes | 4 percent |
| no | no | none on this ground |

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

At a level whose target turnaround is 25 business days, that target counted in calendar days comes to 35 calendar days. A piece taken in 50 calendar days ago with a payment standing on its work order takes 9 percent; with no payment standing, 4 percent. A piece taken in 20 calendar days ago with a payment standing takes 4 percent; with no payment standing, no step is added on this ground.
